title: Make The Practical Plan
objective: Make the pupil’s practical project plan covering promotion, recruitment, resources, risk and feedback, using feasible arrangements and the pupil’s own decisions.

blocks.text: Silver · Unit 2 · Part 2B · Make the practical plan.
Your arts project has a purpose and a personal leadership role. Now you will work out how people can take part and how the activity can run safely and usefully.
Part 2B needs a practical plan for promotion, recruitment, resources, risk and feedback. These areas connect: a change in the activity or group may affect several parts of your plan.
Keep your own choices and name what still needs checking. A written plan is not proof that people have joined or that the project has been delivered.

This deck directly evidences Silver Unit 2 Part 2B, Plan practical issues. Source of award requirements: tools/artsaward/SPEC.json, Silver and universal rules. Silver is the Level 2 Award in the Arts, with TWO units evidenced separately. Mark parts P / A / N. ONE Attempted allowed PER UNIT. Any Not Attempted = Below Pass. Results are Pass / Below Pass only. The 20-file cap applies across the whole Silver portfolio, not per unit or lesson. Keep both units and all parts separately identifiable. Nine cumulative part files or two unit files with part sections are optional layouts, not award requirements. Every locator names the actual file plus page, slide or timecode. The four assessment areas are art form knowledge and understanding, creativity, planning and review, and communication. Only an adviser trained at Silver may assess. Delivery is through a validated centre; staff must confirm both conditions, which this deck does not assert are met. Advisers must not write plans, reviews or evidence for pupils. Read, prompt or scribe the pupil’s exact words and check them back without improving them. Core, Extend and Challenge vary support within Silver; each retains the full evidence meaning and the pupil’s own choices. Keep adult models and source quotations distinct from the pupil’s evidence. No forced private disclosure, public performance, filming or posting. Fourteen forty-minute lesson spines do not deliver the whole 95-hour programme; record actual additional guided and independent work.

Silver Unit 2 Part 2B requires promotion, recruitment, resources, risk and a feedback plan. Use each pupil’s genuine 2A project and role. Prepare accurate information about available materials, spaces, time and access support. Staff confirm local risk and safeguarding procedures, material suitability and any consent or permission actually needed. The deck does not assert arrangements, bookings or approval as completed. No public showing, paid purchase, numbered quota, Gantt chart, receipt set or signed witness form is imposed as an award requirement. Model a practical decision before pupil planning. Adults retain their setting responsibilities while the pupil makes and records their own appropriate project decisions. Invitations remain drafts unless real sending is separately agreed through the setting. Safe sample materials can support a small feasibility test. Preserve earlier plan versions before changes. Later collaboration and delivery decks will test and use the plan; do not claim that planning alone evidences delivery.

stages.title: Arrival · retrieve

blocks.text: Open your own project and role plan from Part 2A. State the arts purpose and the responsibility you will lead. These will guide the practical choices you make today.
List what is already known about possible people, materials and space. Then list what still needs checking. Keep a confirmed fact separate from a hope or a question.

Choose a practical issue that could stop the project working as intended. Perhaps learners need a clearer invitation, a different tool grip or more space for wet work. Explain how the issue connects to your actual activity.

stages.data-ta1: Use real project plans and verified local constraints. Do not invent a room, participant agreement or stock quantity. Accept spoken planning and exact scribing.

stages.title: Starter · create the need

blocks.text: Imagine a clear arts activity with no way for learners to hear about it. Now imagine an inviting message with no materials ready. Either gap could prevent people from taking part.
Promotion explains the opportunity and why it may interest people. Recruitment is how you invite willing people and find out who can take part. They connect, but they are not the same task.

Resources include materials, tools, space, time and useful support. Risk planning considers what could cause harm and what will reduce that risk. Feedback planning sets out what you need to learn and how to ask.
A practical plan turns each area into a decision and an action. It should be clear enough for you and another person to use when preparing the project.

stages.data-ta1: Teach the five terms through the pupil’s projects. Keep risk discussion tied to actual activities and setting procedures; do not frame a worksheet as permission to proceed.

stages.title: I Do · model

blocks.text: Watch me plan a model print activity. The arts purpose is to help learners explore repeated shapes. I work through each practical area rather than writing a vague note to get everything ready.

For promotion, I draft a short invitation explaining the activity and how to ask about access. For recruitment, I choose an agreed way to invite a willing group and check responses. No invitation has been sent in this model.
For resources, I list backing paper, print tools, washable paint, table covers, drying space and support. I check what is actually available before deciding the activity’s scale.
For risk, I notice that spilled paint could make the floor slippery. I plan to keep trays on a stable covered table and use the setting’s spill procedure. Staff must check the real arrangement.
For feedback, I plan to ask learners which choice helped their pattern work. They could point to a print and explain, so the question fits the arts purpose.

blocks.title: Turn an issue into an action
blocks.caption: A practical decision should lead to a clear next action.
blocks.alt: NEED: what the project needs. CHOICE: a workable response. CHECK: facts and agreement. ACTION: who does what next. A practical decision should lead to a clear next action.

blocks.text: These are model decisions, not your plan. A display, collage or other project will need choices that fit its own people, materials and purpose.

stages.data-ta1: Model all five required planning areas explicitly with no claim of agreed arrangements. The safety example is illustrative; apply the actual setting’s procedures and staff responsibilities.

stages.title: We Do · everyone commits

blocks.text: Match these cards to PROMOTION, RECRUITMENT, RESOURCES, RISK, or FEEDBACK. Each card describes a practical planning decision rather than a completed event.

items: 1. A short message explains what the group will make and how to ask about joining.
2. I will use an agreed route to invite willing learners and check who can attend.
3. I will check the number and condition of the print tools before deciding the group size.
4. I will plan where wet work goes so it does not block the walking route.
5. I will ask learners to point to a choice in their work and say what helped them.
6. I will check that a grip aid and enough table space are available.

blocks.text: The key is PROMOTION: 1; RECRUITMENT: 2; RESOURCES: 3 and 6; RISK: 4; FEEDBACK: 5. A decision can affect another area too, but identify its main job here.
Which card would need revisiting if the group became larger? Explain a link between two areas instead of changing only one word in the plan.

stages.data-ta1: Take individual responses before revealing the key. Accept justified cross-links after the main sort. All cards and their key are visible; no separate card pack is assumed.

stages.title: I Do 2 · connect

blocks.text: I check whether my plan is ready to use by pairing a known fact with an unresolved action. This prevents an empty question from looking like a completed arrangement.

blocks.title: Keep facts separate from actions
blocks.caption: An unchecked plan point stays visible until it is resolved.
blocks.alt: CHECKED NOW: available tools and space, real facts with a source. NEXT ACTION: who will confirm the gap, what happens if it changes. An unchecked plan point stays visible until it is resolved.

blocks.text: Suppose the actual stock check shows fewer tools than I hoped. I could reduce the group, use turns or choose a different method. I compare those options with the arts purpose before deciding.
Then I revisit recruitment, resources and timing. A smaller group changes who can join. Turns may require another activity while learners wait. One practical choice can affect the whole plan.
I also test my feedback question. Did you like it? may give a quick view, but asking what helped a learner make a pattern gives more useful evidence about my project aim.

stages.data-ta1: Use a clearly conditional stock example, not an invented count. Model a reasoned revision and retain the earlier plan. Feedback should fit the pupil’s actual aim without imposing a response quota.

stages.title: We Do 2 · lab

blocks.text: Check a resource or instruction for your actual project with an adult or partner. You might inspect a tool, test a paper join or read your draft invitation aloud.
Ask whether the plan gives enough information for someone to take part. Can they understand the art activity, find the next step and request useful access support?
Record the result of the real check and the change it suggests. If an arrangement cannot be checked now, identify who needs to confirm it. Keep that point open until the answer is known.

stages.data-ta1: Provide a genuine small feasibility check with safe materials or a draft instruction. This is preparation, not claimed recruitment or delivery. Record the pupil’s own finding and decision.

stages.title: Independent · evidence

blocks.text: Create the practical plan for your own project. Cover promotion, recruitment, resources, risk and feedback. Use the five headings on a page or make an equivalent clear spoken or visual plan.
For each area, state your choice and the next action needed. Identify who is responsible and what needs agreement. Explain a decision that helps your arts purpose or the people taking part.

items: Core: use the five headings, prompts and an exact scribe. Make your own choices for promotion, recruitment, resources, risk and feedback, keeping checked facts and pending actions clear.
Extend: organise the same five required areas in your own format, with workable actions, responsibilities and reasons.
Challenge: retain all five areas and compare two responses to a practical constraint. Explain your choice and update each area affected by it.

blocks.text: Keep the draft invitation and feedback question with your plan where useful. They are preparation materials, not evidence that invitations were sent or feedback was collected. Save the earlier version before revising it.

stages.data-ta1: All routes retain the complete five-area practical plan and pupil decisions. Scribe only exact words. Staff check real safety and access arrangements before activity; do not fill the pupil’s plan with adult-authored choices.

stages.title: Exit · check the trail

blocks.text: Point to each of the five planning areas. Which action is ready for the next preparation stage, and which needs a real answer first? Keep a clear distinction between the two.
Save the plan under Silver Unit 2 Part 2B. Add the actual file name plus page, slide or timecode. Retain the earlier project and role plan so your practical decisions can be traced to its purpose.
Choose a next action to test with the team. Your plan will need to respond to what happens in real preparation and delivery. Do not mark an arrangement complete just because it appears on a page.

stages.data-ta1: Verify the actual plan location and all five areas. Carry unresolved matters into real preparation. Keep the part evidence cumulative within the whole-Silver cap and distinguish planning from later delivery.

print.intro: Plan the practical details of your chosen arts project: promotion, recruitment, resources, risk and feedback. Record your own decisions and what still needs checking.
focusRows: Promotion and recruitment: my message, route, willing people and pending agreement
Resources and risk: actual checks, access, safe arrangements and responsibilities
Feedback: what I need to learn, how and when I will ask, and my next actions
Actual Silver Unit 2 Part 2B file name plus page, slide or timecode
tiers: Core: use five headings and access help to record your own promotion, recruitment, resources, risk and feedback decisions.
Extend: keep the same five-area plan with clear actions, responsibilities and reasons.
Challenge: retain all five areas, compare responses to a constraint and explain the linked changes.
checks: My plan covers promotion and recruitment for the actual project.
I have planned resources and risk with real checks or clear pending actions.
My feedback question and method link to the arts purpose.
The decisions are my own and proposals are not labelled as completed actions.
The practical plan has an actual file name and page, slide or timecode.
